subject: Handoff: Dedicated GPU pool provisioning + autoscale plan for HelioHealth
content:
From: Alex Kapoor <alex.kapoor@heliohealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: priya.sen@heliohealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning dedicated capacity for inference in prod

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move from POC to a dedicated pool for our inference endpoints. High-level asks: 6xA100-ish equivalent capacity regionally in us-west for primary traffic, warm standby in us-east, ability to burst +50% for business hours, and KV cache persistence for sessions. We also need clear autoscale SLOs so our latency stays under 250ms p50 for short-text scoring.

Can someone from Implementation provide a provisioning plan and a list of what you need from us (network, firewall, cloud account, SOC evidence)?

—Alex

Alex / Grace —

Thanks — I can take the provisioning. Draft plan below and I’ll share a worksheet this afternoon:

- Estimated initial pool: 6xA100-equivalent instances in us-west-2 (zone spread across two AZs)
- Warm standby: 2xA100-equivalent in us-east-1 kept at idle with fast failover (route 53 failover)
- Networking: customer-managed VPC peering (we'll need a CIDR range and peering request)
- IAM/KMS: request for service principal and KMS key ARN for model artifacts
- Storage: S3 bucket write access for model artifacts and checkpointing (lifecycle rules TBD)
- Timeline: kick off provisioning 5/24, validate 5/26, canary rollout 5/28, full handoff 6/01

I'll attach the provisioning checklist and region-capacity-matrix once updated. If Helio needs a faster timeline, call out constraints and we can negotiate burst policy versus reserved commit.

-Marissa

Attachment: provisioning-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)

-----Original Message-----
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Alex Kapoor <alex.kapoor@heliohealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Dedicated capacity scoping for HelioHealth

Quick note on autoscale/burst:

- Baseline scaling: target 6 active instances, with autoscale floor = 4 and ceiling = 12 (ceil = up to +100% to match burst needs).
- Burst model: instant burst using pre-warmed spare capacity within the reserved pool for +50% sustained over 1 hour, and ephemeral burst to cloud spare capacity for spikes up to +100% for <15 minutes (subject to pricing).
- Ramp policy: reactive scale-up on 95th-percentile CPU or model-latency breach, with 30s evaluation window; scale-down with cool-down 15 minutes to avoid flapping.
- Cost control: enforce per-model concurrency limits and token-rate caps to protect baseline SLA.

I'll put these into a policy doc and include cost delta estimates.

-Rishi

-----Original Message-----
From: Alex Kapoor <alex.kapoor@heliohealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Dedicated capacity scoping for HelioHealth

Thanks, Marissa/Rishi — this looks good. Couple clarifications: 

1) For burst to cloud spare capacity (ephemeral), can you confirm expected throttling behavior and whether we get any prefailure warnings?
2) For KV cache persistence: we want session affinity for 48 hours; will that require external Redis or can Redwood persist in-pool?
3) Any constraints that would affect our compliance team (SOC2 evidence, audit logs retention)?

We'd like to keep the canary small (1 model endpoint, 10% traffic) and confirm rollback steps prior to 5/28.

—Alex

-----Original Message-----
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Alex Kapoor <alex.kapoor@heliohealth.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: Dedicated capacity scoping for HelioHealth

Alex —

Answers inline: 

1) Ephemeral burst: policy will include a throttling threshold and circuit-breaker; customers receive a pre-failure alert (we emit events at 80% pool utilization) and an automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant if required. Throttling is applied per-endpoint once pool capacity hits 100% and we recommend token-rate caps to smooth spiky traffic.

2) KV cache: Redwood can persist KV cache in-pool for up to 24 hours; for 48-hour affinity we recommend an external Redis/managed cache in the customer's VPC (we provide the connector and guidance). We'll add the Redis deployment to the checklist.

3) Compliance: SOC2 artifacts (control matrix, exception logs) can be shared via our secure drive link once NDA is signed. Audit logs retention for Dedicated is configurable; default 90 days, with options for extended retention as a paid add-on. Please send an inventory of specific documents the Helio compliance team needs.

I'll also attach the updated region-capacity-matrix with expected AZ spread and failover plan.

-Monica

Attachment: region-capacity-matrix.csv (csv, 12KB)
